newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian hijacker captured, hostages freed - official.
newsitem.headline: Russian hijacker captured, hostages freed - official.

text.p: Police on Monday seized an armed hijacker who had been holding about 30 hostages in the south Russian region of Dagestan for almost four hours, a spokesman for the local interior ministry said.
The spokesman said the nobody had been hurt in the incident.
The incident came to an end at about 4.45 p.m. (1245 GMT) when the gunman was captured alive, after having earlier released all hostages, the official said.

The unidentified man, armed with an assault rifle and a hand grenade, seized the hostages on a bus heading for the town of Kizlyar when he forced the driver to turn around and stop about 10 km (seven miles) outside Dagestan's capital, Makhachkala, officials said.
The hijacker had demanded a helicopter, the interior ministry said. But officials could not confirm an Itar-Tass new agency report than the man was also seeking $100,000 in ransom.

Hijackings have not been uncommon in Russia's turbulent North Caucasus. Many have involved Chechens fighting for independence for their mainly Moslem region but others have been staged for ransom or unplanned responses to police searches.
